I appreciate you sharing that, but I'm not going to change my view just because it's a minority position. Majority opinion isn't evidence — it's just a snapshot of what people currently believe. There were times when the majority believed the Earth was flat, or that smoking was harmless. Popularity doesn't determine truth.

I'm also a little wary of the framing here. "Everyone I know disagrees" is meant to make me feel like an outlier, but that doesn't actually address the substance of my argument. I laid out real concerns — anxiety, polarization, attention fragmentation. Those don't go away because they're unpopular.

I'm happy to discuss this further, but I'd rather engage with the actual ideas than count votes. What specifically do you think I'm getting wrong?
